mode: isolated read-only snapshot; source/Git/state mutation guard

issues.reason: The review gate builds its diff and changed-file list from `git diff HEAD` and `git diff --name-only HEAD`. Neither command includes untracked files, so any new file the Implementation Agent creates outside `milestone.sourceFiles` and outside `tests/` is missing from both the diff and the sources. That code is then built and committed by checkpoint (`add -A`) without ever being reviewed. This breaks the requirement that the independent review covers the entire candidate before a verified checkpoint.
issues.requiredChange: Get the changed-file set from `treeStatus`/`git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` together with `git diff --name-only HEAD`. Include the full content of untracked files in the review context, for example by listing them explicitly alongside the diff. Add a workflow test showing that an agent-created file outside `sourceFiles` reaches the reviewer.

issues.reason: `previousReview` is picked by sorting `.harness-state/reviews/*.json` by name and taking the last entry. The names are random UUIDs, so the file chosen has nothing to do with recency, the current milestone, or the failure being retried. On top of that, `state.failure` survives the revision-change reset in `openWorkflow`, so stale or unrelated review feedback can be handed to a different milestone. The Implementation Agent therefore gets nondeterministic feedback that isn't tied to its target AC.
issues.requiredChange: Record the failing review's run ID (or artifact path) together with its milestone in State when a review gate fails. Pass that structured result only when retrying the same milestone, and clear it on checkpoint, replan, or revision reset. Remove the directory scan.

issues.reason: `sourceContext` adds the size of every file, binaries included, to the 800 KB budget before deciding to send only a `[binary file]` placeholder. A full regression passes every tracked `src/`/`tests/` file (verify.ts:58), so any mod with ordinary texture/PNG assets totalling more than 800 KB always fails the review gate. That makes completion unreachable for realistic projects. Each milestone review also includes every file under `tests/` regardless of relevance.
issues.requiredChange: Check for binary content before adding to the budget, and count only the bytes actually placed into the context. Restrict regression and milestone review sources to text files that are relevant (changed files plus declared `sourceFiles` and test mappings) instead of all of `tests/`. Add a test with a large binary asset.

issues.reason: `verifyIdHistory` treats an item as retired only when its own body contains `Status: retired`. `parseProject`, by contrast, also makes the children of a retired Feature inactive. The two disagree on what retirement means, so a child of a retired Feature that is later deleted and reintroduced is not caught as ID reuse at the moment of retirement.
issues.requiredChange: Compute the active ID set from `parseProject(...).items.filter(i => i.active)` (or apply the same parent propagation) so both use one retirement definition.

issues.reason: The snapshot only covers Git-visible files inside `.harness`, so ignored Harness files such as `.harness/dist` (the code actually being executed) and ignored project files are not guarded. The comment says build outputs are not agent inputs, but `dist` is the running Harness.
issues.requiredChange: Include `.harness/dist` (or all of `.harness` except `node_modules`) in the snapshot, or document this as an explicit limitation in the README.

issues.reason: `.harness-state/runs/<runId>.json` duplicates `manifest.json`, adding only `projectHash`, which is just `specHash` again. Its comment claims it keeps the reviewed source of truth, but it doesn't. `readVerification` (verify.ts), `hasProjection` (projector.ts) and `writeExecutable` (project.ts) are never used.
issues.requiredChange: Remove the duplicate runs record and its misleading comment, and delete the unused exported helpers.

issues.reason: `applyChanges` compares HEAD before and after its own synchronous file writes. Harness performs no Git operation in between, so the check can never fail. Mutation by the agent is already guarded by the snapshot in `callAgent`.
issues.requiredChange: Remove the `beforeHead`/`head` comparison.

issues.reason: Several modules use dynamic `await import('node:fs/promises')` for functions from a module they already import statically: `mkdir` in state.ts, `realpath` in git.ts:15-17, and `readdir` in workflow.ts:175. This is pointless indirection. Separately, `initProject` calls `capability()` twice when it generates the config (project.ts:73-76) and serializes JSON by hand instead of using `json`.
issues.requiredChange: Use the static imports, call `capability` once, and use `json()` to write the config.

issues.reason: `scanLogs` scans configured client logs under `mct-home` that persist across runs and are never truncated or offset. Errors from earlier runs therefore fail later runs indefinitely, and the scan doesn't measure the current run alone.
issues.requiredChange: Record each configured log's size at runtime start and scan only the bytes appended during this run, then copy that slice into evidence.

issues.reason: The workflow allowlist includes `config`, which can write repository configuration such as `core.hooksPath` or remotes. It is only used to read `.gitmodules`.
issues.requiredChange: Allow only read forms of `config` (for example, require `--file .gitmodules --get-regexp`), or move that one read into an explicit, narrow call.

issues.reason: No tests cover: an invalid spec-edit output leaving `PROJECT.md` untouched and uncommitted; review context containing new untracked files; previous review feedback selection; forced server kill or runtime log error failing the run; or plan `sourceFiles` outside the implementation scope (these currently fail only later, in `sourceContext`).
issues.requiredChange: Add fake-executable tests for these paths, and validate `sourceFiles` against `allowedImplementationPath` in `validatePlan`.

rounds.resolution: Untracked review context, structured retry identity, binary budget, mutation guards, log offsets, Git allowlist and test coverage fixed; dead helpers removed.

issues.reason: validateEvidence works out the required gates and per-AC verification types from the CURRENT spec for every AC in a historical checkpoint. Example: checkpoint M01 covers AC-1 and AC-2. A chat request then adds `gametest` to AC-2, and AC-1 stays verified because its fingerprint is unchanged. validateProject then calls validateEvidence for M01. That call now requires a gametest gate and AC-2/gametest evidence that the old run never produced, so it throws. chatProject calls validateProject right after its commit, and openWorkflow calls it at every start. The project is then stuck: every validate/plan/develop/regression fails, and no Harness command can recover it.
issues.requiredChange: When validating a historical checkpoint, check only the ACs that are still verified against that runId/checkpoint. Compute the required gates from those ACs only, and check evidence for them against the checkpoint's recorded verification. ACs in the checkpoint that changed or are now pending must not affect the check. Add a workflow test: two ACs in one milestone, then a chat that changes one AC's Verification list, then validateProject/develop succeed.

issues.reason: The Implementation Agent receives sources only for milestone.sourceFiles, yet it must return complete file contents. tests/verification.json and tests/e2e/manifest.json are shared across all milestones, and verify.ts always sends them to the reviewer. The implementer does not get them unless the planner happens to list them. A later milestone that adds its own mapping without seeing the existing file will overwrite earlier ACs' mappings or scenarios. Those ACs then fail final regression ("No tests/verification.json mapping"), which resets every AC to pending.
issues.requiredChange: Always include tests/verification.json and tests/e2e/manifest.json in the implementation sourceContext, as the review gate already does. Add a test with two milestones that checks the first milestone's mapping survives.

issues.reason: For the 'regression' milestone, the review gate sends every tracked src/, tests/ and build file to Claude. sourceContext throws above 800 KB and callAgent above 1 MB, with the message 'narrow sourceFiles'. Regression has no sourceFiles to narrow, so any moderately large mod can never reach `complete`. The task's regression list (compile, unit, build, GameTests, runtime, E2E, visual, persistence, multiplayer, log scan) does not include a full-repository AI review. Each checkpointed milestone's diff was already reviewed. A whole-repo review also lets unrelated non-deterministic findings fail regression and reset every AC.
issues.requiredChange: Drop the AI review gate from regression, and in validateEvidence stop requiring 'review' when milestone === 'regression'. Alternatively, keep the review but bound it to a defined, size-safe input and document that. Add a test for regression on a source tree larger than the context limit.

issues.reason: When shutdown fails, the error becomes an AggregateError whose message is only 'Runtime/shutdown failed'. verify() records only error.message, so state.failure and the evidence manifest lose both the scenario failure and the shutdown cause.
issues.requiredChange: Build the message from the underlying errors' messages, e.g. join them with '; ', so failure records stay actionable.

issues.reason: doctor reports codex/claude as available after checking only a few flags. codexArgs/claudeArgs also rely on --ephemeral, --ignore-rules, --disable, --skip-git-repo-check, --output-last-message, --tools, --strict-mcp-config, --setting-sources and --no-session-persistence. A CLI missing any of these is shown as available and then fails at runtime.
issues.requiredChange: Derive the required flag list from the flags codexArgs/claudeArgs actually emit, so doctor checks exactly the contract that is used.

issues.reason: The Phase values 'visual', 'persistence' and 'multiplayer' (also listed in state.schema.json) are never set; the visual, persistence and multiplayer checks run inside the 'e2e' gate. Config.gradle.client is detected and stored but never used. These are dead states and config that add concepts without behavior.
issues.requiredChange: Remove the unused Phase enum values and the unused gradle.client config, or actually drive phases from them. Do not keep both.

issues.reason: checkpoint() re-implements the gate and evidence checks that verify() has just enforced and that validateEvidence() runs again on the next line. That is three copies of the same acceptance rule, which can drift apart.
issues.requiredChange: Keep the candidate-snapshot comparison and validateEvidence as the single authority for evidence acceptance, and delete the duplicated inline gate/evidence loops.

issues.reason: Two problems. First, a relative --harness-repo (./ or ../) is passed to `git submodule add` with cwd=destination, so it resolves against the new project rather than the user's working directory. Second, `rev-parse <ref>^{commit}` in a fresh clone cannot resolve non-default branch names, because those exist only as origin/<name>.
issues.requiredChange: Resolve a local --harness-repo with path.resolve before use. Resolve templateRef explicitly, either as a commit or tag or via refs/remotes/origin/<ref>, and fail clearly when it is ambiguous. Add tests for both cases.

rounds.resolution: Partial historical checkpoint verification, shared manifest context, bounded regression, diagnostics, doctor flags, driven phases and template ref/local-path handling fixed.

issues.lines: verifyIdHistory (observe/parseProject over every first-parent PROJECT.md revision)
issues.reason: The ID-reuse check fully validates every historical revision of PROJECT.md with the current parser. Several normal situations make that throw. (1) An existing project already has a PROJECT.md in a different format in its Git history. (2) A user committed an intermediate draft, for example a Feature that has no AC yet, which parseProject rejects even with Status: draft. (3) A later Harness submodule bump tightens the parser. Once any of these revisions is in history, validateProject, and therefore validate/status/plan/develop/regression/chat, fails permanently. Git history cannot be fixed without rewriting it. This breaks HAR-AC-014 (an existing project plus init gives the same contract) and turns one bad commit into a project that can never be validated.
issues.requiredChange: Only the full validation of the current PROJECT.md should be strict. For historical revisions, collect the ID set with a lenient heading-only extraction: sectionsOf plus the F-/R-/AC- heading patterns and the item's own Status: retired line. Do not run the whole parseProject structural validation on old revisions. Add a test where history contains an unparseable or incomplete PROJECT.md revision and validate still succeeds and still detects ID reuse.

issues.reason: For manual spec edits, the documented path is `validate --refresh-projections`, which runs invalidate() and keeps unchanged-fingerprint ACs verified, followed by a user commit. That commit changes HEAD, and openWorkflow then resets every AC to pending. So the selective invalidation is never reached for manual edits. Docs/README say only changed or affected ACs lose their verified status. The behavior is safe, but it contradicts the docs and needlessly forces re-verification of everything.
issues.requiredChange: Either document that any out-of-band commit, including a manual spec commit, resets all verification, or keep verified state when the only difference between state.revision and HEAD is PROJECT.md (checked with git diff --name-only) and the fingerprints are unchanged.

issues.reason: This adds a second subprocess path next to the run/success boundary. It uses different error handling and size limits, and the Git hooks/fsmonitor hardening is not applied consistently. project.ts also calls run('git', ['check-ignore', ...]) directly instead of going through the guarded git() wrapper.
issues.requiredChange: Send Git invocations through one boundary. For example, let run optionally return the stdout Buffer for blob reads, and use git() with an allowed nonzero exit for check-ignore.

issues.reason: files.size is the same for every file in the loop, so it carries no information. The saved artifact names cannot be traced back to the client log they came from.
issues.requiredChange: Name each saved log excerpt after its source log (for example, its basename or its index in config.logs).

issues.reason: relativePath reads like a function that computes a path, but it is a void assertion that throws.
issues.requiredChange: Rename it to something like assertSafeRelativePath.

issues.reason: Every Gradle invocation uses --rerun-tasks. As a result, the build gate re-runs compile and the full test suite after the static and unit gates have already run them, so the tests run twice per milestone and twice in regression. The declared reports are already deleted beforehand, so --rerun-tasks is only needed on the test/GameTest tasks to prevent stale results.
issues.requiredChange: Keep --rerun-tasks only for the test and gameTest tasks, where report freshness matters, or document why the build gate needs a full rerun.

rounds.resolution: Lenient historical ID extraction with inherited retirement, conservative manual commit invalidation documentation, one Git process boundary including binary blobs, traceable log names, assertion naming and Gradle rerun scope fixed.

rounds.scope: Changed files and all six remaining findings

issues.reason: Gradle's --rerun-tasks flag applies to the whole task graph it runs, not only to the task named on the command line. So the unit and GameTest gates still recompile and reprocess resources for every dependency. That repeats the compile work the static gate already did. docs/verification.md says only the unit/GameTest tasks are forced to rerun, which is slightly inaccurate. The finding is still resolved: the build gate no longer reruns tests, and the reports stay fresh. This is a leftover inefficiency, not a correctness regression.
issues.requiredChange: Use Gradle's task-scoped `--rerun` option (Gradle 7.6+), placed right after the test or GameTest task, so only that task is forced and its dependencies stay up-to-date. If you keep --rerun-tasks, change docs/verification.md to say the whole graph of those gates is rerun.

rounds.resolution: Verdict pass. Minor documentation issue resolved by explicitly stating that --rerun-tasks also executes the test task dependency graph.

rounds.scope: Requested canonical-spec refinements, nearly deterministic inference, external PROJECT.md template and removal of unused product sections and partial-plan exclusions

issues.reason: New `--reference` paths are only checked after `openWorkflow` and `setPhase('spec_edit')`, and the check runs inside the try block. A mistyped or forbidden reference path is plain user input, but it goes through `fail()`. `fail()` sets phase to `failed` and clears `state.regression`. A project that was `complete` loses its complete status and needs a new full regression, which starts Minecraft at runtime cost. Nothing about the product or source has changed. The new test only checks that PROJECT.md and HEAD stay the same, so it misses this.
issues.requiredChange: Resolve and check `sourceContext(root, referenceFiles)` (including the null/missing check) before `setPhase(root, state, 'spec_edit')` and outside the `fail()` handler, so an invalid reference leaves the saved state alone. In the missing/forbidden reference test, also assert that the prior phase and regression record are unchanged.

rounds.resolution: Pass with one minor issue: invalid reference input could clear complete/regression. Moved reference validation before the state transition and failure handler; regression test now asserts the entire saved complete state remains unchanged.
